arxiv-1910-14124.title: Bayesian causal inference via probabilistic program synthesis
arxiv-1910-14124.creator: Sam Witty, Alexander Lew, David Jensen, Vikash Mansinghka
arxiv-1910-14124.description: Abstract Causal inference can be formalized as Bayesian inference that combines a prior distribution over causal models and likelihoods that account for both observations and interventions. We show that it is possible to implement this approach using a sufficiently expressive probabilistic programming language. Priors are represented using probabilistic programs that generate source code in a domain specific language.

arxiv-2102-11233.creator: Chunhua Geng, Traian E. Abrudan, Veli-Matti Kolmonen, Howard Huang
arxiv-2102-11233.description: Abstract In this paper, we study probabilistic time-of-arrival (ToA) and angle-of-arrival (AoA) joint localization in real indoor environments. To mitigate the effects of multipath propagation, the joint localization algorithm incorporates into the likelihood function Gaussian mixture models (GMM) and the Von Mises-Fisher distribution to model time bias errors and angular uncertainty, respectively.

arxiv-2304-00491.title: A Complete classification of two-dimensional endo-commutative algebras over an arbitrary field Thanks: emails: 1 96asrorovdiorjon@mail.ru; 2 uralbekbaev@gmail.com; 3 isamiddin@uitm.edu.my
arxiv-2304-00491.creator: D.Asrorov, U.Bekbaev, I.Rakhimov
arxiv-2304-00491.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by D.Asrorov, U.Bekbaev, I.Rakhimov. In the paper we describe the class of all 2-dimensional endo-commutative algebras over any basic field. Thereby, we extend S.-E. Tsukada’s recent description of the class of all 2-dimensional endo-commutative algebras over ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} to any basic field, where the concept of endo-commutative algebra was first introduced and motivations to study this class of algebras also had been given. We give canonical representatives of the isomorphism classes such algebras in dimension two over any basic field.

arxiv-2310-01547.title: On the near-optimality of betting confidence sets for bounded means
arxiv-2310-01547.creator: Shubhanshu Shekhar, Aaditya Ramdas
arxiv-2310-01547.description: Abstract Constructing nonasymptotic confidence intervals (CIs) for the mean of a univariate distribution from independent and identically distributed ( i.i.d. ) observations is a fundamental task in statistics. For bounded observations, a classical nonparametric approach proceeds by inverting standard concentration bounds, such as Hoeffding’s or Bernstein’s inequalities.

arxiv-2504-21355.creator: Christian Vaquero-Stainer 1,2, Tymoteusz Miara 2, Anne Juel 2, Matthias Heil 3, Draga Pihler-Puzović 2
arxiv-2504-21355.description: Abstract There has been much recent interest in the chiral motion of achiral particles that sediment in a viscous fluid in a regime where inertial effects can be neglected. This occurs in a broad range of applications such as those involving biological objects like algae, ultra-thin graphene flakes, or colloidal suspensions.

arxiv-2601-16355.creator: Suhong Moon, Minwoo Kang, Joseph Suh, Mustafa Safdari, John Canny
arxiv-2601-16355.description: Abstract Humans act via a nuanced process that depends both on rational deliberation and also identity and contextual factors. In this work, we study how large language models (LLMs) can simulate human action in the context of social dilemma games.

pmc-10737042.title: EXAMINING THE NON-LINEAR ASSOCIATION BETWEEN YEARS OF EDUCATION AND LATE-LIFE COGNITION
pmc-10737042.creator: Sara Robinson, Jason Salemi, Hongdao Meng, Judith Rijnhart
pmc-10737042.description: Dementia, a rising health concern, is expected to impact 13 million adults in the United States by 2050. Low education is a well-established risk-factor for dementia. However, few studies have investigated possible non-linearity of the association between years of education and late-life cognition, nor have investigated gender differences in this association.

pmc-11506324.title: Cellular Profile of Subfornical Organ Insulin Receptors in Mice
pmc-11506324.creator: Han-Rae Kim, Jin-Kwon Jeong, Colin N Young, Myron R Szewczuk
pmc-11506324.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Brain insulin receptor signaling is strongly implicated in cardiovascular and metabolic physiological regulation. In particular, we recently demonstrated that insulin receptors within the subfornical organ (SFO) play a tonic role in cardiovascular and metabolic regulation in mice. The SFO is a forebrain sensory circumventricular organ that regulates cardiometabolic homeostasis due to its direct exposure to the circulation and thus its ability to sense circulating factors, such as insulin.

pmc-11599939.title: Effect of a weight loss diet with or without Spirulina supplementation on serum lipids and antioxidant capacity of overweight dogs
pmc-11599939.creator: Davide Stefanutti, Lorenzo Serva, Michele Berlanda, Federico Bonsembiante, Gianfranco Gabai, Erica Franceschinis, Marco Cavazzoni, Giada Morelli, Rebecca Ricci
pmc-11599939.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Obesity is a major health issue in dogs associated with disturbances in lipid metabolism and oxidative stress. Spirulina has been shown to have hypolipidemic and antioxidant effects in various animal species. No such data regarding dogs are available, however. The present study aimed to investigate the effect of a therapeutic high-protein, high-fiber weight loss diet, with or without Spirulina supplementation, on biochemical parameters of overweight dogs, with particular reference to serum lipids and plasma antioxidant capacity.

pmc-12610361.creator: Ganna Nevoit, Maksim Potyazhenko, Ozar Mintser, Gediminas Jarusevicius, Alfonsas Vainoras, Yumay Chen

pmc-13227696.title: Effect of fabrication technique on surface roughness and color stability of novel resin occlusal veneers after thermomechanical aging: an in-vitro study
pmc-13227696.creator: Ahmed Rizk Ali Mostafa, Badawy Abo El Mahasen Badawy, Mervat Mourad Roushdy
pmc-13227696.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundResin-based occlusal veneers are increasingly used within minimally invasive restorative dentistry. However, evidence remains limited regarding whether fabrication technique (subtractive milling versus additive 3D printing) influences clinically relevant surface characteristics particularly surface roughness and color stability after thermomechanical aging.MethodsEighteen resin occlusal veneers were fabricated from the same standardized digital design (STL) using NanoKsa G-Plus material and divided into two groups (n = 9): milled CAD/CAM and 3D-printed.

pmc-13596068.title: Normal gains: estimators of learning rates in pretest-posttest settings
pmc-13596068.creator: Jairo A. Navarrete-Ulloa, Valentina Giaconi, Gonzalo Contador
pmc-13596068.description: IntroductionNonlinear transformations of pretest and posttest scores are widely used in educational and psychological measurement to estimate group-level change, yet the statistical behavior of estimators derived from such transformations under measurement error remains poorly understood. We examine this problem in the context of normalized gains (ngains), a ratio-based transformation used to estimate group-level “learning rates” in pretest-posttest designs.
